spec: Given exactly 10 digits as a string, format them into a US-style phone number '(XXX) XXX-XXXX'.
reference:
def format_phone_number(digits):
    return f"({digits[0:3]}) {digits[3:6]}-{digits[6:10]}"

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Format a Celsius temperature value as a string with exactly one decimal place followed by the degree Celsius symbol '°C'.
reference:

spec: Pluralize an English noun using simple rules: words ending in s, x, z, ch, or sh get 'es' appended; words ending in a consonant followed by y have the y replaced with 'ies'; all other words simply get 's' appended.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Format a count with a noun, using the singular form of the word when the count is exactly 1 and otherwise pluralizing it with simple English rules (s/x/z/ch/sh get 'es', consonant+y becomes 'ies', otherwise add 's'), producing a string like '3 cats'.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Convert a simple plural English noun back to its likely singular form: words ending in 'ies' (with more than 3 letters) become 'y'; words ending in 'ses', 'xes', 'zes', 'ches', or 'shes' drop the trailing 'es'; other words ending in 's' (but not 'ss') drop the final 's'; anything else is returned unchanged.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a count and explicit singular and plural word forms, return a string combining the count with the singular form when the count is exactly 1, or the plural form otherwise.
reference:
def format_count_noun(n, singular, plural):
    return f"{n} {singular if n == 1 else plural}"

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Join a list of strings into a natural-language list: an empty list gives an empty string, a single item is returned as-is, two items are joined with ' and ', and three or more items are comma-separated with 'and' before the final item (Oxford comma style).
hidden_tests: assert format_list_with_and(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']) == 'a, b, c, and d'
assert format_list_with_and(['one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five']) == 'one, two, three, four, and five'
assert format_list_with_and(['cat', 'dog', 'bird', 'fish']) == 'cat, dog, bird, and fish'
assert format_list_with_and(['north', 'south', 'east', 'west']) == 'north, south, east, and west'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a template string with {field} placeholders and a list of record dictionaries, render the template once per record by substituting each record's field values, and return the list of rendered strings in the same order as the records. Assume every placeholder has a matching key in every record.
hidden_tests: assert mail_merge('Dear {name}, age {age}', [{'name': 'Sue', 'age': 30}, {'name': 'Max', 'age': 25}]) == ['Dear Sue, age 30', 'Dear Max, age 25']

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a template string containing one or more '___' blank markers and a list of words, replace each blank with the next word from the list, in order, and return the filled string. Assume the number of blanks matches the number of words.
visible_tests: assert fill_blanks('The ___ jumped over the ___.', ['cat', 'fence']) == 'The cat jumped over the fence.'
assert fill_blanks('___ is here', ['Sam']) == 'Sam is here'
hidden_tests: assert fill_blanks('Start ___ middle ___ end', ['x', 'y']) == 'Start x middle y end'
assert fill_blanks('___, ___, and ___', ['red', 'green', 'blue']) == 'red, green, and blue'
assert fill_blanks('no markers here', []) == 'no markers here'
assert fill_blanks('The ___ is ___.', ['sky', 'blue']) == 'The sky is blue.'
assert fill_blanks('A ___ B ___ C ___ D', ['1', '2', '3']) == 'A 1 B 2 C 3 D'
assert fill_blanks('multi ___ blank ___ test ___', ['1', '2', '3']) == 'multi 1 blank 2 test 3'

spec: Capitalize only the first character of a string, leaving the rest of the string unchanged. An empty string is returned unchanged.
hidden_tests: assert capitalize_sentence('  leading space') == '  leading space'
assert capitalize_sentence('x y z') == 'X y z'
assert capitalize_sentence('!start with punctuation') == '!start with punctuation'
assert capitalize_sentence('multiple words here now') == 'Multiple words here now'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a paragraph made of sentences separated by '. ' (period then space), capitalize the first letter of each sentence and rejoin them with '. '.
visible_tests: assert capitalize_sentences('hello world. this is a test.') == 'Hello world. This is a test.'
assert capitalize_sentences('one sentence only') == 'One sentence only'
assert capitalize_sentences('first. second. third.') == 'First. Second. Third.'
hidden_tests: assert capitalize_sentences('a. b. c.') == 'A. B. C.'
assert capitalize_sentences('already Capped. still fine.') == 'Already Capped. Still fine.'
assert capitalize_sentences('multiple. short. sentences. here.') == 'Multiple. Short. Sentences. Here.'
assert capitalize_sentences('no period at all here') == 'No period at all here'
assert capitalize_sentences('start. middle sentence here. end.') == 'Start. Middle sentence here. End.'
assert capitalize_sentences('lower. UPPER. mixed.') == 'Lower. UPPER. Mixed.'
assert capitalize_sentences('first sentence. second sentence.') == 'First sentence. Second sentence.'
assert capitalize_sentences('one. two. three. four.') == 'One. Two. Three. Four.'
assert capitalize_sentences('z. y. x.') == 'Z. Y. X.'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: In a multi-line text, collapse any run of three or more consecutive newline characters down to exactly two newlines (one blank line), leaving single and double newlines unchanged.
hidden_tests: assert remove_extra_blank_lines('no newlines here') == 'no newlines here'
reference:
def remove_extra_blank_lines(text):
    import re
    return re.sub(r'
{3,}', '

', text)
